purpose: Make full-scope mapping a pre-authoring thinking tool that exposes coverage, evidence, representation use, and template-driven repetition without treating repetition itself as a defect.
required_for: Any build spanning multiple items, sections, forms, or resource instances where the builder is authoring new learning/evidence content rather than merely rendering an already-finalized canonical set.
pre_authoring_gate: Resolve every exact I-can across the complete requested scope before final student materials are authored.

For each I-can, map the evidence job, natural DOK, likely misconception(s), source-supported question families, representations/data/phenomena/models, and the student reasoning/action that actually matters.

Use the dedicated question-design taxonomy to map best-fit quantitative/formula, vocabulary, representation, multi-step, misconception, and response-mode variety for each I-can; do not impose universal percentages.
Plan destination coverage from the I-can mini-banks, then reconcile section inventory totals.
Read the complete map as a whole and repair zero-coverage, unsupported overconcentration, or suspicious template clusters before rendering.
purposeful_repetition: Keep repetition when it serves a mapped purpose such as fluency, retrieval, repeated independent evidence, consistent comparison across forms, repeated use of a high-value representation, or deliberate return to an important structure.
accidental_repetition: Flag repetition when the same question shell, experience sequence, representation choice, reasoning suffix, or student action recurs mainly because it is easy to template/render rather than because the learning architecture calls for it.
decision_rule: When repetition looks suspicious, ask what mapped learning/evidence purpose it serves. If the purpose is real, keep it. If the repetition is only a template byproduct, revise the PLAN before authoring final resources.
no_quota_rule: Do not impose anti-repetition quotas such as 'no structure more than twice.' The goal is intentionality, not maximum variety.
late_audit_distinction: This pre-authoring map review is NOT a late anti-clone/diversification pass. After authoring, do not launch broad cosmetic rewrites merely to lower repetition; repair actual alignment, security, evidence, representation, or quality defects.
course_specific_reflection: The unit/section is a container; the exact I-can is the atomic planning address. Do not let a large section inventory hide a thin or missing I-can bank.
Do not convert I-can-first into a new quota system. In a 24-item Practice set with three I-cans, 8/8/8 is not the default; evidence need determines the split.

Purposeful repetition means repeated evidence families with meaningful variation. Reusing the exact finished student prompt across canonical destinations is normally cloning, not purposeful repetition.
Repeated formula/procedure families, qualitative prediction patterns, or recurring phenomenon-analysis structures may intentionally recur when they serve the Physics learning job.
Use the map to see whether sections that need phenomena, diagrams, measurement, data, experimental setup, model revision, or explanation actually use those forms; do not impose a visual/lab quota.

A prediction-observation-model-revision sequence is powerful when the phenomenon calls for it, but it must not become the automatic shell for every investigation/performance merely because it is easy to template.

Parallel family design should vary the actual evidence path when useful (unknown quantity, dependency path, representation, misconception, or response mode), not merely object names or sentence order.
